Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Energy Holdings Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to request through the phone keypad by pressing star then one. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Energy Holdings' Q2 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Jennifer Hayes, Chief Strategy Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Technology Officer; Karen Lopez, Chief Regulatory Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Communications Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong earnings per share performance and key drivers, positive updates on regulatory rate case filings and outcomes, excellent generation fleet performance and availability, favorable authorized versus earned return on equity dynamics, clear earnings guidance for the next quarter and full year, advances in grid modernization and smart grid initiatives, disciplined capital expenditure planning and project updates, and strong comparisons of current period results to prior periods and guidance.

Let me provide some more detail on these eight key aspects. On EPS, we saw robust growth from revenue expansion and efficiencies. Regulatory progress included key approvals boosting revenues. Our fleet hit high availability marks across thermal, nuclear, and renewables. ROE gaps are narrowing with better recovery. Guidance remains on track with upside. Grid investments are enhancing reliability. Capex is focused on growth projects like renewables and T&D. And results beat prior periods handily.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to discuss the financials.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mike. Good morning, everyone. For the second quarter, we reported earnings per share of $1.52 and revenue of $4.2 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Let me unpack our EPS performance and the key drivers behind this quarter's standout results. On an adjusted basis, we delivered $1.52 per share, a 7% increase from $1.42 in Q2 2023 and 4.5% from Q1 2024. This exceeded consensus of $1.48 and the top of our guidance. Year-to-date adjusted EPS is $2.98, on pace for the midpoint of our full-year range of $5.80 to $6.20.

The positives included strong revenue growth across segments from higher retail electricity sales and favorable power pricing. Retail sales volumes rose 4.1% to 28.5 terawatt-hours, surpassing the U.S. utility average, led by 12% commercial demand from hyperscale data centers adding 300 megawatts contracted, with 1.2 gigawatts in negotiations for AI workloads. Residential sales increased 2.8% with hotter cooling degree days up 15% year-over-year in key areas. In unregulated generation, contributing 35% of earnings, merchant prices averaged $45 per megawatt-hour, up 10%, with 85% hedged at $42 realized.

Operational efficiencies and cost discipline added about $0.08 to EPS. O&M expenses fell 5.2% to $650 million via fleet optimization, improving gas turbine capacity factors to 68%, nuclear uprates, forced outages to 4.1%, early coal idlings cutting fuel costs 8%, and predictive maintenance reducing wind downtime 20%. Regulatory tailwinds from rate cases and incentives, like a $250 million annual increase with 10.25% ROE adding $0.05 quarterly, IRA PTC/ITC on 400 megawatts solar-plus-storage for $0.03, and AFUDC on transmission capex.

Headwinds were managed: depreciation up 9% to $850 million from capex, interest up $40 million but cost of debt at 4.2%, tax rate to 22.5%, minimal share dilution from repurchases. Southeast drove 55% earnings growth, Midwest margins up 15%, Texas batteries at 95% availability. This supports our Reliable Renewables transformation, 45% emissions-free portfolio targeting 60% by 2028, with data center demand at 8-10% CAGR.

Turning to authorized versus earned ROE, for the trailing 12 months, consolidated authorized ROE is 10.25%, up 25 basis points from rate settlements recognizing higher capital costs. Earned ROE is 9.12%, a 113 basis point gap or $285 million under-recovery on $25.2 billion equity base, narrower sequentially. Jurisdictional breakdowns show New York at 9.80% authorized versus 9.05% earned due to DER investments; Pennsylvania 10.50% vs 9.45% from nuclear uprates; Virginia 10.20% vs 9.35%; Maryland 9.95% vs 8.95%; FERC transmission 10.75% vs 9.65%. Northeast gaps tightest, progress from rate filings and O&M optimization lifting earned ROE 72 basis points year-over-year. Initiatives like AMI, solar-storage, reliability enhancements, and nuclear uprates are closing it, targeting 50 basis points gap by 2026 for 6-8% EPS growth.

On earnings guidance, for Q3 we expect adjusted EPS of $1.55 to $1.65. Revenues $2.85 to $2.95 billion up 7%, EBITDA $1.05 to $1.12 billion up 6%, O&M $650-680 million, capex $950 million. Full year raised to $5.75-$5.95 EPS, revenues $11.6-11.9 billion up 6-8%, EBITDA $4.45-4.65 billion. FCF $1.8-2.0 billion before growth capex, total capex $4.0 billion. Assumptions include GDP 2.1%, gas $3.00-3.40, IRA credits. Pillars: VPPs, SMRs, regional tailwinds. Risks: weather, regulatory lag.

Our capex plan for 2024 is $2.8 billion, up 12%, five-year $14.5 billion at 7-9% rate base CAGR. Generation $1.1 billion including $650 million renewables: Prairie Wind Farm Phase II 450 megawatts COD, Solar Canyon 600 megawatts solar-plus-storage, gas peakers, nuclear extensions. T&D $1.4 billion for reconductoring, Eastern Backbone upgrade, dynamic ratings. Other $300 million EV infra, CCUS. Funded balanced, ROIC 9.5%.

Finally, Q2 comparisons: revenues up 8.2% year-over-year and 4.1% sequentially, EBITDA up 12.4% and 6.8%, EPS up 16.2% and 5.4%. Regulated up 7.5% revenues, 10% EBITDA from rates and load. Generation up 12% revenues, 18% EBITDA from gas dispatch, batteries. YTD ahead, raised FY guidance: revenues $10.1-10.4 billion, EBITDA $3.25-3.35 billion, EPS $4.85-5.00. Q4 merchant strength supports.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $950 million, primarily focused on renewables and grid hardening. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate continued EPS growth in line with our long-term algorithm.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Let me provide an update on the operational front. Our fleet-wide equivalent availability factor reached 93.2% in Q2, up 210 basis points year-over-year, best since 2019, above industry averages. Net generation 42.8 TWh up 5% quarter-over-quarter.

Thermal: CCGTs at 96.8% EAF, heat rates 6,450 Btu/kWh, outages 1.2%. Coal 91.5% EAF. Nuclear 97.1% capacity factor. Renewables: wind 38.2%, solar 24.5%, batteries 95% with $35 million ancillaries. PJM 94.5%, MISO recovered, ERCOT scarcity strong.

Drivers: AspenTech digital twins across 80% thermal slashing costs 12%; hydrogen readiness $150 million; nuclear uprates 120 megawatts. Targeting 94-95% for 2024, supporting net-zero with coal retirements, offshore wind, hybrids.

We are seeing improved efficiency in our combined cycle gas plants due to digital twin implementations. This has resulted in a 5% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 60% on key units.

Jennifer Hayes: Thank you, David. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery storage and small modular reactor space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the Texas market.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Jennifer. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. Over five years, $1.2 billion deployed, 92% smart assets, SAIDI down 22% to 78 minutes, SAIFI 18% to 0.9.

ADMS with GE GridOS for volt/VAR, FLISR saving $4.5 million Q2. AMI 98% coverage, 12% peak reduction. DERMS manages 450 megawatts, 25% curtailment efficiency. Midwest VPP pilot 50 megawatts to 200; Texas PMUs cut events 35%; California microgrids $150 million. Cybersecurity zero-trust $80 million. EV 120,000 chargers off-peak 15%.

Accretive at 14% IRR, $350 million 2024 capex up 12%, 5-7% EPS accretion. We've recently deployed advanced OT monitoring to enhance defenses and are piloting dynamic line ratings in Texas.

Karen Lopez: Thank you, Sarah. On the regulatory front, we've filed five major rate cases past 12 months, three settled favorably this quarter. Texas PUCT approved $5.2 billion rate base up 14%, $452 million revenue increase, 9.8% ROE, formula updates. Midwest ICC $320 million on $3.9 billion base, 9.6% ROE, EV rider $150 million. California settlement $285 million annual, 10.1% ROE. FERC $65 million plus $400 million allocation.

Lag down to 9 months, $1.25 billion approved YTD, two more Q4 filings $600 million. Supports 6-8% growth, ROE to 9.7%. We received approval for our transmission rider in Texas. This will allow us to recover $1.8 billion in investments.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Karen. We are pleased to announce that our community outreach program in the Atlanta metro area has resulted in a 25% increase in positive sentiment towards Nexus Energy Holdings.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Lisa, David, Jennifer, Sarah, Karen, and Robert. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for renewables expansion?

Mike Thompson: Certainly. We're accelerating with projects like Prairie Wind Phase II at 450 megawatts COD, Solar Canyon 600 megawatts hybrid by H2 2025, targeting 3 gigawatts renewables and storage by 2027, leveraging IRA credits for 12% plus IRRs, paired with data center PPAs.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez: What is your outlook for EPS guidance?

Lisa Chen: Our Q3 guidance is $1.55 to $1.65, full year raised to $5.75 to $5.95, reflecting load growth, renewables contributions, merchant strength, with 6-8% long-term growth on capex returns and rate outcomes.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee: How are you mitigating risks related to fuel volatility?

David Patel: Through hedging 85% at $42 per MWh, digital twins reducing outages 15%, battery ancillaries $35 million quarterly, nuclear baseload at 97% factors, and CCUS pilots for gas units qualifying for 45Q.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: What is the anticipated impact of recent rate cases on your earnings?

Karen Lopez: The Texas order alone adds $452 million annualized or about $0.10 quarterly EPS, California $285 million, Midwest $110 million full year, totaling $1.25 billion YTD revenue approvals flowing through positively with minimal lag.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q2, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Nexus Energy Holdings for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Nexus Energy Holdings.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
